agent_notes: Two Nahors: the grandfather (TIPNR Nahor@Gen.11.22-Luk, v.22-25) and Terah's son (person.nahor, v.26+). Kept separate as the registry proposes.

11:26 says Terah lived 70 years and begat Abram, Nahor and Haran; it does not say Abram was the eldest or born at 70. Terah's death at 205 (11:32) against Abram's departure at 75 (12:4) only works if Abram was born when Terah was 130 (Acts 7:4 sequence); at 70 Abram would be 135 at Terah's death. I keep the 70 reading for the chain, as the packet's anchor note allows, and the anchor margin already covers the 130 reading.

agent_notes: The text gives no date for Babel. I place it a century after Peleg's birth (MACRO_ERA, margin 30 years) because 10:25 says the earth was divided 'in his days', and evt.gen_10.earth_divided stands at c. 2238 BCE, about 120 years after Peleg's birth. Whether 'divided' means the scattering of Babel is the traditional reading (Ibn Ezra on 11:10 ties Peleg's name to the division), but it is an identification, so I link no causal edge to evt.gen_10.earth_divided. The 100-year offset is a guess within that range; the durations of the children (a year of settling, five years of building, a year of scattering) are likewise estimates with no textual figure.

history.note: [consider] Address the relation to evt.gen_10.nimrod_kingdom in the temporal note. Either accept that the Gen 10 dating is not in sequence and say so, or move the episode so that Babel exists before Nimrod rules from it (the margin could then reach back past 2389 BCE). (GEN.10.10: "the beginning of his kingdom was Babel … in the land of Shinar"; GEN.11.2: "they found a plain in the land of Shinar; and they dwelt there"; GEN.11.9: "Therefore is the name of it called Babel")

agent_notes: Haran's death in Ur (11:28) is undated. It precedes Terah's departure from Ur and the text puts it before the marriages (11:29, where Milcah, Haran's daughter, marries Nahor); I place it 20 years after Abram's birth with a margin of 15 years, MACRO_ERA. This is an estimate only. Pseudo-Jonathan's story of Abram in the furnace and Haran's burning is not in the Hebrew and is not used.

agent_notes: 11:29–30 gives no ages. I assume the marriages some 30 years after Abram's birth (margin 15 years). Sarai's barrenness (11:30) is a state, kept in this event; it carries into Gen 12–21. A later chapter (Gen 21) will fulfil the promise of a child, not this verse.

evt.gen_10.peleg_born already dates this same birth (10:25) at c. 2358 BCE; this event is the same birth reached through the Gen 11 ages (Flood + 2 + 35 + 30 + 34 = 101 years). The two should agree within a year; compare them in review.

The actual construction between the plan (11:3–4) and God's descent (11:5, 'which they had built') is not narrated and has no event of its own; the five-year gap between the plan and the descent is my estimate. The Targum Pseudo-Jonathan additions on 11:4 (idolatrous worship at the tower's top, weapons for war) are not in the Hebrew and are not used.

Chain follows the Masoretic ages and the packet's anchor note: 2 + 35 + 30 + 34 + 30 + 32 + 30 + 29 + 70 = 292 years from the Flood's start to Abram's birth. The chain gives Abram's birth at anchor.flood + 292 years, which equals anchor.abraham_birth (2166 BCE) by construction, so the two agree. 'Two years after the flood' (11:10) is taken from the Flood's start year (anchor.flood), as the anchor's own basis does. Births anchor on the father's birth START rather than on the parent's START, so that each age is read off the father; the parent is only the grouping span. Shem's age of 100 (11:10) is not a separate event.
Terah's birth is derived: Nahor was 29 at Terah's birth (11:24).

Terah's age at death, 205, is counted from his own birth (terah_born). Compare the result with the departure of Abram in Gen 12:4 at 75 (anchor.abraham_birth + 75 years): with Terah born 222 years after the Flood and dying 205 years later, his death is 427 years after the Flood, 135 years after Abram's birth on the 70-year reading; this is the known Terah-age problem, flagged here for the reviewer.

The date of the departure from Ur is not given; per the reviewer, I keep the whole window before Abram's 75th year: 55 years after Abram's birth, margin 15 years, with 12:4 as the upper bound. Haran's death (11:28) is not written as a cause of the departure: the text gives no reason, though Lot, Haran's son, travels with Terah. With Abram leaving Haran at 75 (12:4, in the Gen 12 chapter) and Terah dying at 205 (11:32), the Masoretic ages leave a conflict if Terah was 70 at Abram's birth (Terah would die when Abram was 135). Ur is read as loc.ur (Ur of the Chaldeans, the same coordinates as Chaldea) and the journey duration is from `urim travel`; if Ur is instead the northern Ur near Haran, the journey is much shorter.

history.note: [should_fix] Keep the whole window before Abram's 75th year, for example offset 55 years with a margin of 15 years, or about 50 ± 20. Say in temporal_reasoning_note that 12:4 is the upper bound. (GEN.12.4: "Abram was seventy and five years old when he departed out of Haran"; GEN.11.31: "they came unto Haran, and dwelt there")

agent_notes: Divine speech 11:7 ('let us go down and confuse their language') is fulfilled at once by 11:8–9 (the scattering and the confusion at Babel). I wrote FULFILLS_PROPHECY from this speech to the scattering event, with a note that the words are a decision and the fulfilment is immediate. Pseudo-Jonathan has the Lord speak to the seventy angels; this does not change the dating.
No location given in the text (probably Ur, but not stated), so left out.
Genealogy events have no event location: the text gives none, so it was left out.
The event ends in Haran, but the place is Ur; Haran and Canaan are MENTIONED as destinations.
The location carries over from the scene at Shinar (11:7 'there'). The 'let us' plural in 11:7 is not modelled as separate participants.

notes.note: Verse 11:27 (the heading 'these are the generations of Terah', naming Terah's sons and Lot) is genealogical framing with no date and is covered by no event; 11:11, 13, 15, 17, 19, 21, 23, 25 ('he lived after… and begat sons and daughters') are covered by the genealogy parent, not by separate events. The remaining-years figures imply each patriarch's death (Shem 600, Arpachshad 438, Shelah 433, Eber 464, Peleg 239, Reu 239, Serug 230, Nahor 148) but the text does not state them as deaths, so I wrote no death events except Terah's, which 11:32 states.
